title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — Rom. 5.13 usque ad legem; γάρ links; I concede the major
pass_a_gloss: Paul: until the law sin was in the world; sin is not imputed when there is no law. You argue: the sin of the prior verse is that pre-law world-sin, clear from the verbal texture and especially γάρ. Placeus grants that major and asks you to remember it—it is true and useful to overturn your view and firm his.
pass_b_english: For, says the Apostle, Until the law sin was in the world. But sin is not imputed when there is no law.
Thus, you say, I argue from this saying of the Apostle.

That sin of which the Apostle speaks in the immediately preceding verse is that sin which was in the world until the law, as is plain from the sequel and texture of the words, especially from that particle γάρ, which is causal.
This I concede, and I ask that you remember it, for it is true, and highly useful for overturning your opinion and establishing mine.
source_text: Nam, inquit Apostolus, Usque ad legem peccatum erat in mundo. Peccatum vero non imputatur, quum nulla lex est. Sic, inquis, ex hoc dicto Apostoli argumentor. Peccatum illud, de quo loquitur Apostolus versu immediate praecedenti, est peccatum illud quod fuit in mundo usque ad legem, ut patet ex sequela & textura verborum, maxime ex illa particula γάρ, quae est rationalis. Hoc concedo, & ut memineris rogo, nam & verum est, & ad tuam sententiam evertendam, meam autem firmandam apprime utile.

choices.choice: Pre-law world-sin = prior-verse sin via γάρ
